mainTopic: Leftover תודה money, replacement animals of a lost תודה or חטאת, and a תודה mixed up with its תמורה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: leftover money from a תודה may buy its לחם, but leftover money from the לחם may not buy a תודה. The גמרא explains this with רב כהנא's teaching that the loaves are called 'תודה', while the תודה is never called 'לחם'. Next, רבא rules on three תודה animals set aside one after another as replacements, and says which of them still need loaves depending on which one was offered. רבי זירא applies the same pattern to חטאות, where the leftover animals either die or graze. In both cases אביי disagrees and says all of them are replacements of one another. רבי חייא then teaches that if a תודה got mixed up with its תמורה and one died, the survivor has no remedy, and the גמרא limits this to someone who said 'הרי זו'. A list of challenges to רבי חייא follows. לוי proposes several fixes before רבי. רבי rejects each one, and his reason for the last rejection comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Leftover money: from the offering to the loaves, but not back
steps.stepSummary: Money left over from buying a תודה may be used for its לחם. Money left over from buying the לחם may not be used for a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he set aside money for his thanks offering and some was left over, he buys loaves with it. If he set aside money for the thanks-offering loaves and some was left over, he may not buy a thanks offering with it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא that gives a one-way rule about leftover money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every תודה comes with loaves (לחמי תודה). Leftover money can move from the animal to the loaves, but not from the loaves to the animal. The rule is not symmetrical, and that is exactly what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks offering, an animal brought together with loaves
The loaves that go with a thanks offering
Were left over (extra money remained)

steps.confusionAlert: This is one-way only. Leftover תודה money can buy loaves, but leftover loaf money cannot buy a תודה animal.

phrases.english: and some was left over — he brings loaves with it.
If he set aside money for the thanks-offering loaves and some was left over —
he may not bring a thanks offering with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that began before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover תודה money may buy the לחם. Leftover לחם money may not buy a תודה.

steps.title: Why does the money only go one way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the one-way rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא's rule works in only one direction. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal and the loaves are one unit, the money should move both ways. The גמרא wants the source that explains why it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason leftover money moves from the תודה to the לחם but not the other way.

steps.title: Suggestion: the loaves are called 'תודה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason is רב כהנא's teaching, from a פסוק, that the loaves themselves are called 'תודה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because of רב כהנא. For רב כהנא said: Where do we learn that the thanks-offering loaves are called 'thanks offering'? As it says: 'Then he shall offer with the sacrifice of the thanks offering loaves of matza.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer from רב כהנא, who learns from a פסוק that the loaves are themselves called 'תודה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the words 'התודה' and 'חלות' sit side by side, so the loaves count as 'תודה'. That means money set aside 'for the תודה' also covers the loaves. The opening word אילימא ('if you say') warns us that this answer is about to be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, a suggestion the גמרא is about to test
From where do we learn it?
Matza loaves

phrases.english: If you say it is because of רב כהנא,
as רב כהנא said:
From where do we learn that the thanks-offering loaves
are called 'thanks offering'?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהִקְרִיב עַל זֶבַח הַתּוֹדָה חַלּוֹת מַצּוֹת״.
phrases.english: As it says: 'Then he shall offer with the sacrifice of the thanks offering loaves of matza.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a possible answer to the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The loaves are called 'תודה', so money set aside for the תודה may also be spent on them.

steps.title: Challenge: then the reverse should work too
steps.stepSummary: If the loaves and the offering share one name, leftover loaf money should also be usable for the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the opposite should also be true!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion: if the two share a name, why not let the money move in both directions?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא's teaching seems to link the loaves and the animal. A link usually works both ways, so it does not seem to explain why the ברייתא allows only one direction.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The reverse too

phrases.english: If so, the reverse should also be true!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using רב כהנא's teaching as the reason for the one-way rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the loaves and the תודה are linked by name, the link should allow money to move both ways.

steps.title: The name only works one way
steps.stepSummary: The loaves are called 'תודה', but the תודה is never called 'לחם', so the money moves only one way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The loaves are called 'thanks offering', but the thanks offering is not called 'loaves'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the name-sharing goes in only one direction, so רב כהנא's teaching does explain the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the loaves 'תודה', so 'money for the תודה' includes the loaves. No פסוק calls the animal 'לחם', so 'money for the לחם' cannot include the animal. A one-way name gives a one-way rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Is called

steps.whatToRemember: Loaves are called 'תודה', but the תודה is not called 'לחם'. That is why leftover money moves only from the animal to the loaves.

phrases.english: The loaves are called 'thanks offering',
but the thanks offering is not called 'loaves'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 and keeps the suggestion from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the derivation to a one-directional name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sharing a name means the money should move both ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק names only the loaves 'תודה', not the reverse, so the money moves one way only.

steps.title: רבא's case of three replacement offerings, offered with the first
steps.stepSummary: Three תודה animals were set aside one after another as replacements, and all three turned up. If the first is offered, the second needs no loaves but the third does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: He set aside his thanks offering and it was lost. He set aside another in its place, and it was lost. He set aside another in its place. Then the first ones were found, and now all three are standing. If he gained atonement with the first, the second does not need loaves, and the third needs loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא describes a chain of three replacement animals and rules on what happens if the first one is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each animal was set aside to replace the one just before it: the second replaces the first, and the third replaces the second. Once the first is offered with its loaves, its direct replacement (the second) needs no loaves. The third replaces the second, and the second was not offered with loaves, so the third still needs loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside (designated an animal as an offering)
In its place, as its replacement
He gained atonement (by offering one of them)
Needs loaves brought with it

steps.confusionAlert: For רבא, each animal replaces only the one right before it. The third is not a replacement of the first.

phrases.english: And רבא said: He set aside his thanks offering and it was lost,
and he went and set aside another in its place, and it was lost,
and he went and set aside another in its place,
and the first ones were found,
phrases.notes: The first two animals, the ones that had been lost.

phrases.english: and now all three of them are standing.
If he gained atonement with the first —
the second does not need loaves,
the third needs loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about תודה loaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the first is offered, the second (its replacement) needs no loaves, but the third does.

steps.title: Offered with the third
steps.stepSummary: If the third is offered, the second needs no loaves, but the first does.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gained atonement with the third, the second does not need loaves, and the first needs loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his ruling for the case where the third animal is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third replaced the second, so once the third is offered with loaves, the second needs none. The first is replaced only by the second, which will now be offered without loaves, so the first still needs loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: The third one

phrases.english: If he gained atonement with the third —
the second does not need loaves,
the first needs loaves;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next scenario in רבא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the third is offered, the second needs no loaves, but the first does.

steps.title: Offered with the middle one
steps.stepSummary: If the middle one is offered, neither the first nor the third needs loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: With the middle one, neither of the two needs loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his last scenario: the middle animal is the one offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle one is linked to both of the others. It replaced the first, and the third replaced it. Since it was offered with loaves, both the first and the third are free from loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle one

steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, an animal is free from loaves only if the animal directly linked to it as replacement or original was offered with loaves.

phrases.english: With the middle one — neither of the two needs loaves;
phrases.notes: 'He gained atonement' is assumed here from the earlier lines, and 'the two' means the first and the third.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's three scenarios.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the middle one is offered, neither the first nor the third needs loaves.

steps.title: אביי: all three replace one another
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that whichever one is offered, the other two need no loaves, because they are all replacements of one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even if he gained atonement with any one of them, neither of the other two needs loaves, since they are all replacements of one another.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי disagrees with רבא and gives one simple rule for all three scenarios.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא linked each animal only to the one right next to it in the chain. אביי sees all three as a single group of replacements for the same original offering. So once any one is offered with loaves, the other two need none.

keyTerms.meaning: Replacements
Of one another

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: each animal replaces only its neighbor in the chain, so the result depends on which one was offered. אביי: all are replacements of one another, so whichever is offered, the other two need no loaves.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן –
phrases.english: אביי said: Even if he gained atonement with any one of them —
neither of the other two needs loaves,
since they are all replacements of one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבא's chain-by-chain ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whichever animal is offered, the other two need no loaves, since all are replacements of one another.

steps.title: רבי זירא applies the three-animal case to sin offerings: atonement with the first
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the same three-replacement pattern applies to חטאות. If the owner gets atonement with the first, the second must die and the third grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא says: The same goes for sin offerings. A man set aside a sin offering and it got lost. He set aside another in its place and that one got lost too. He set aside a third in its place. Then the first two were found, so now all three are standing. If he got atonement with the first, the second must be left to die, and the third goes out to graze.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא takes the case we just learned about three תודה animals and moves it over to חטאות. He starts with the case where the first animal is the one offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a חטאת, the question is not about loaves. It is about what happens to the leftover animals: some are left to die and some are put out to graze until they get a blemish. The second must die because the first, which it was replacing, already brought atonement. The third grazes because it was a replacement for the second, and the second was never offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering, brought to atone for an accidental sin
He set aside (an animal for a specific offering)
He got atonement (through offering one of the animals)
Must be left to die (it cannot be offered or used)
Goes out to graze until it gets a blemish, then it is redeemed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the תודה case. Here the result is 'dies' or 'grazes', not 'needs loaves' or 'doesn't need loaves'. The pattern of who replaces whom is the same, but the outcome is different.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira says:
And so too regarding sin offerings:
he set aside his sin offering and it was lost,
and he set aside another in its place, and it was lost,
and he set aside another in its place,
and the first ones were found,
so now all three of them are standing.
If he got atonement with the first:
the second must die, and the third grazes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן חַטָּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries the three-replacement pattern from תודה (steps 6-9) over to חטאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Atonement with the first חטאת: the second dies and the third grazes.

steps.title: Atonement with the third sin offering
steps.stepSummary: If the owner gets atonement with the third, the second dies and the first grazes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he got atonement with the third, the second must die, and the first grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא continues with his second case: this time the third animal is the one offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second must die because the third was its replacement, and the third was already offered. The first only grazes, because its own replacement, the second, will never be offered. This matches the order of the תודה case in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: The third (animal)
The first (animal)
The second (animal)

phrases.english: If he got atonement with the third:
the second must die, and the first grazes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case in רבי זירא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Atonement with the third חטאת: the second dies and the first grazes.

steps.title: Atonement with the middle sin offering
steps.stepSummary: If the owner gets atonement with the middle animal, both the first and the third must die.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he got atonement with the middle one, both of the others must die.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives his last case: the middle animal is the one offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle animal is connected to both of the others. It was the replacement for the first, and the third was set aside as its replacement. So once the middle one is offered, both of the others are 'covered', and both must die. This matches the תודה case in step 8, where neither one needed loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle one
Both of them
They must die

phrases.english: If he got atonement with the middle one:
both of them must die.
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means the first and the third.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case in רבי זירא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Atonement with the middle חטאת: the first and the third both die.

steps.title: אביי: whichever one is offered, the other two die
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that no matter which חטאת brings atonement, the other two must die, because all three are replacements of each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: Even if he got atonement with any one of them, the other two must die, because they are all replacements of one another.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי disagrees with רבי זירא's detailed breakdown, just as he did in the תודה case in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא follows a chain: each animal replaces only the one right before it. אביי sees all three as one group of replacements for the same original offering. So once any one of them is offered, the other two have no purpose left and must die.

keyTerms.meaning: Replacements, substitutes
Of each other
Even

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא: replacements form a chain, so the result depends on which one was offered. אביי: all of them are replacements of each other, so whichever one is offered, the others die.

phrases.english: Abaye says:
Even if he got atonement with any one of them,
the other two must die,
since all of them are replacements of one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי זירא's case-by-case results.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whichever חטאת is offered, the other two die.

steps.title: Why did רבי זירא need to say 'and so too'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point רבי זירא is making with 'וכן', since it looks like the same rule as the תודה case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and so too'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask why רבי זירא had to teach this at all. This sets up the next step, which will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's three cases follow the same pattern as the תודה cases. So the גמרא wants to know what we would have gotten wrong if he had not said it.

keyTerms.meaning: What (is meant by)
And so too, the same way

phrases.english: What is the point of 'and so too'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why רבי זירא's statement was needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point the word 'וכן' teaches beyond the תודה case.

steps.title: Sin offerings cannot be added voluntarily, yet the rule is the same
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the תודה rule works only because a person may bring extra תודות. A person cannot bring extra חטאות, so maybe the rule would be different. רבי זירא teaches that it is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: There, with the תודה, we can say 'he is just adding more תודות.' But here, we cannot say 'he is adding more חטאות,' so I would say the rule does not apply. That is why he teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. It shows the mistake we might have made if רבי זירא had not said 'וכן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תודה case, the third animal still needed loaves. You could explain that by saying a person is allowed to bring as many תודות as he wants, so the extra animal is just one more. But no one can bring a חטאת as a free-will gift, so we might have thought the third חטאת must die. רבי זירא teaches that it grazes, because it really is the replacement of the second, just as in the תודה case.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Adding more thanks offerings (bringing extra ones by choice)
I would say no (the rule does not apply)
He teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the replacement rules come from how replacements work, not from a person's ability to bring extra offerings by choice.

phrases.english: You might have said:
it is there that one can say
'he is one who adds more thanks offerings,'
phrases.notes: A person may bring as many תודות as he likes, so the extra animal could count as just one more.

phrases.english: but here, where one cannot say
'he is one who adds more sin offerings,'
I would say no.
So he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָתָם הוּא דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'וכן'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without רבי זירא, we might have said the third חטאת dies, since no one can add extra חטאות. He teaches that it is still treated as the second's replacement and grazes.

steps.title: A thanks offering mixed with its substitute: the survivor has no remedy
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that if a תודה got mixed up with its תמורה and one of them died, the one left has no fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: A thanks offering got mixed up with its substitute, and one of them died. The other one has no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching connected to the משנה's rule that a תודה's substitute does not need loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real תודה needs loaves, and its תמורה does not. Once the two are mixed up, we cannot tell which one survived. So we do not know how to offer it.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks offering, brought together with loaves
Got mixed up
Substitute: an animal someone tried to swap in for a holy animal, which also becomes holy
Remedy, a way to fix the situation

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
A thanks offering that got mixed up with its substitute,
and one of them died,
the other one has no remedy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: תּוֹדָה שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבָה בִּתְמוּרָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic tied to the משנה's rule that a תמורה of a תודה needs no loaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a תודה is mixed with its תמורה and one dies, the survivor has no remedy.

steps.title: Why there is no remedy: loaves or no loaves, either choice could be wrong
steps.stepSummary: Bringing loaves might be wrong if it is the תמורה. Not bringing loaves might be wrong if it is the תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should we do? If we bring loaves with it, maybe it is the substitute. If we don't bring loaves with it, maybe it is the thanks offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי חייא's ruling by showing that both choices run into a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the surviving animal is the תמורה, bringing loaves with it would be wrong. If it is the real תודה, leaving out the loaves would be wrong. Since we cannot know which one it is, there is no safe way to offer it.

keyTerms.meaning: What should we do?
We should offer / bring
The loaves that come with a תודה
Perhaps

steps.whatToRemember: A mix-up between a תודה, which needs loaves, and its תמורה, which does not, leaves no way to offer the survivor. Either choice might be wrong.

phrases.english: What should we do?
Should we offer loaves with it?
Perhaps it is the substitute,
Should we not offer loaves with it?
Perhaps it is the thanks offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי חייא's ruling of 'no remedy'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both bringing loaves and not bringing loaves could be wrong, so the survivor cannot be offered.

steps.title: What case is רבי חייא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: If the owner said 'עלי', he could bring another animal with loaves and cover both possibilities, so why does רבי חייא say there is no fix?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he said 'It is on me', he has to bring another animal and loaves anyway. So let him say: if the animal still alive is the תמורה, then this new animal is the תודה and these are its loaves. If the animal still alive is the תודה, then these are its loaves, and this new animal is just a backup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא's ruling by showing a fix that seems to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone says 'עלי', he owes a תודה no matter what happens. Here the extra animal plus loaves covers both options. If the live animal is the תמורה, the new animal is the real תודה and takes the loaves. If the live animal is the תודה, it takes the loaves, and the new animal is only a backup, which needs no loaves. So how can רבי חייא say there is no fix?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the exact case?
'It is on me'. A personal promise to bring an offering, so he stays responsible if it is lost.
A backup animal set aside in case the first one is lost. It does not need loaves.
Its loaves, the bread brought with a תודה

steps.confusionAlert: The loaves go with only one animal: whichever one is the real תודה. If the standing animal is the תמורה, the new animal takes the loaves. If the standing animal is the תודה, the new animal is just a backup and takes no loaves.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he said, "It is on me",
he has no choice but to bring
another animal and loaves,
and let him say:
If the one still standing is the substitute,
this one is the thanks offering, and these are its loaves;
if the one still standing is the thanks offering,
these are its loaves, and this one will be a backup!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חייא's 'no fix' ruling from steps 16-17 by offering a fix for the עלי case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's ruling that the remaining animal has no fix
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the עלי case, an extra animal with loaves covers both possibilities, so there should be a fix.

steps.title: The case is where he said 'הרי זו'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא is talking about someone who set aside one specific animal ('הרי זו'), so he owes no backup and the fix does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where he said, 'This animal is a תודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חייא's ruling is about a different kind of promise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'הרי זו' the obligation sits only on that one animal. He owes nothing if it is lost. So the trick of bringing another animal does not help, because he has no duty to bring a backup. The fix only worked because 'עלי' makes him owe a תודה no matter what.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not needed except for...'. It shows which case a ruling is really about.
'This one is...'. Setting aside one specific animal, with no duty to replace it.

steps.whatToRemember: 'עלי' means he owes it no matter what, so a backup is possible. 'הרי זו' means only this animal, so there is no backup and no fix.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he said, "This one is [a thanks offering]."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by limiting רבי חייא to the הרי זו case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא's ruling seemed to cover even someone who said עלי, where a fix exists.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא means someone who said הרי זו. There he owes no backup, so the fix does not work.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming challenges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives code words to remember the sages and the topics of the challenges that come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: למודים, מידת, עלה, שיש, שכן, דדמה, דאי; חלש, מותר, תמורה, בחוץ, חזקיה, הפריש חטאת, לאחר יותר.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is a memory list that sets up the series of challenges to רבי חייא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group of words hints at the sages who ask: לוי (called למדין), רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא, עולא בר אבא, רב שישא, רב אשי and רב כהנא, רב דימי, and רבינא. The second group hints at the topics, like חולין and שלמים, leftover, substitute, and outside.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid: code words to help remember a list

phrases.english: (Memory aid: Lemudim, Middat, Ila,
phrases.notes: This is just a memory aid, code words for the sages who will ask next. It isn't part of the argument, and some versions leave out these words in round brackets.

phrases.english: Sheyesh, Sheken, Dedamah, De'i,
Ḥalash, leftover, substitute, outside,
phrases.notes: These words now switch to hinting at the topics of the questions. חלש stands for חולין and שלמים.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya, separated a sin offering, for a guarantee.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Transition line that introduces a new series of challenges to רבי חייא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It is a memory list for the challenges to רבי חייא that follow.

steps.title: לוי suggests bringing loaves on a condition
steps.stepSummary: Bring loaves and say: if the live animal is the תודה, these are its loaves; if not, they become plain food.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said before רבי: Let him bring loaves and say, 'If the animal still standing is the תודה, these are its loaves. If not, let them become plain, unholy food.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first challenger, לוי, offers a fix that would solve רבי חייא's problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the problem is the loaves: bringing them might be wrong, and leaving them out might be wrong. לוי says to bring them on a condition. If they are not needed, they simply turn into ordinary bread. That seems to remove both risks.

keyTerms.meaning: A title for לוי, meaning a learned one, used when he spoke before רבי
Ordinary, unholy food

phrases.english: Lemedin said before Rabbi:
phrases.notes: Lemedin is לוי, and רבי is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: But let him bring loaves and say:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָךְ דְּקָיְימָא תּוֹדָה הִיא – הָא לַחְמָהּ,
phrases.english: If the one still standing is the thanks offering, these are its loaves;
if not, let them go out to be ordinary food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לְמֵדִין לִפְנֵי רַבִּי: וְלַיְתֵי לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first challenge in the series announced by the memory aid in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's ruling of 'no fix' and the loaf problem from step 17
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bringing loaves on a condition, so they become plain food if not needed, avoids both risks.

steps.title: We may not bring plain food into the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: רבי rejects the condition: the loaves must be waved in the עזרה, and if they turn out to be plain food, he has brought חולין into the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Do we bring ordinary food into the Temple courtyard?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers לוי and shows why his fix does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves of a תודה are taken into the עזרה. If the live animal turns out to be the תמורה, those loaves were ordinary food all along. Bringing ordinary food into the עזרה is not allowed, so the condition does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple courtyard
Bringing ordinary food into the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: The ban on bringing חולין into the עזרה blocks many 'conditional' fixes, and it comes up again across קדשים.

phrases.english: He said to them:
And do we bring ordinary food into the Temple courtyard?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: וְכִי מַכְנִיסִין חוּלִּין לָעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects לוי's conditional fix from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the suggested fix breaks another rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Conditional loaves would solve the problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loaves might turn out to be חולין, and חולין may not be brought into the עזרה, so רבי חייא's ruling stands.

steps.title: Bring a second animal with loaves, and the extra one becomes a peace offering
steps.stepSummary: לוי suggests bringing another animal with loaves. If the animal standing here is the תמורה, the new animal is the תודה with these loaves. If the standing animal is the תודה, the loaves are its loaves and the new animal becomes a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him bring another animal and loaves and say: if the animal standing here is the substitute, then this new one is the thanks offering and these are its loaves. If the animal standing here is the thanks offering, then these are its loaves and this new one will be a peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי suggests a new fix: bring a second animal together with loaves, and set a condition so that whichever animal turns out to be the real תודה, the loaves belong to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 rejected bringing loaves alone, because the loaves might end up as חולין in the עזרה. This plan avoids that problem, because the loaves are a true לחם תודה either way. If the new animal is not needed as the תודה, it becomes a שלמים, which needs no loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute animal that took on holiness when the owner tried to swap it for a קרבן
Thanks offering, which is brought with loaves
Peace offering, which needs no loaves
Its loaves, meaning the loaves that go with the תודה

phrases.english: And let him bring an animal and loaves,
phrases.notes: He means a second, new animal, on top of the one already standing there.

phrases.english: and let him say:
if that one which is standing here is the substitute,
then this is the thanks offering and these are its loaves;
if that one which is standing here is the thanks offering,
then these are its loaves
and this one will be a peace offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an improved version of the plan in step 21, built to avoid the חולין problem raised in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that there is no fix for the remaining animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second animal with conditions covers both possibilities, so the loaves are always valid לחם תודה.

steps.title: Rejected: it cuts short the eating time of the peace offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי rejects the plan, because the new animal might really be a שלמים, yet it would be eaten under the shorter time limit of a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: because he is reducing the eating time of the peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers that this fix does not work, because it shortens the time allowed for eating the שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שלמים may be eaten for two days and one night, but a תודה only for one day and the night after it. Nobody knows whether the new animal is the תודה or a שלמים, so it must be eaten by the shorter deadline. That cuts down the eating time of an animal that might really be a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Reduces or cuts short
Eating, here meaning the time allowed for eating a קרבן

phrases.english: He said to them:
Because he is reducing
the eating of the peace offering.
phrases.notes: A שלמים gets two days and a night, a תודה only a day and a night. Being unsure forces the shorter deadline.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a new legal problem that the suggested fix creates.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making the extra animal a שלמים solves everything.
steps.terutzMaskana: It does not work, because the possible שלמים would lose part of its eating time.

steps.title: Bring a second animal, and the extra one becomes leftover of a thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: לוי changes the plan: if the standing animal is the תודה, the new animal becomes a מותר תודה. A מותר תודה needs no loaves, and it has the same eating time as a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said to רבי: let him bring another animal and loaves and say: if the standing animal is the substitute, this new one is the thanks offering and these are its loaves. And if the standing one is the thanks offering, these are its loaves and this new one will be the leftover of a thanks offering.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי fixes his plan. Instead of calling the extra animal a שלמים, he calls it a מותר תודה, so its eating time matches that of a תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in step 24 was the shorter eating time of a תודה. A מותר תודה is eaten like a תודה, so that problem goes away. It is also brought without loaves, so the plan still covers both possibilities.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover of a thanks offering: an extra animal set aside for a תודה, which is brought without loaves

phrases.english: Levi said to Rabbi:
And let him bring an animal and loaves,
and let him say:
if that one which is standing here is the substitute,
then this is the thanks offering and these are its loaves;
and if this one which is standing here is the thanks offering,
then these are its loaves
and this one will be the leftover of a thanks offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵוִי לְרַבִּי: וְלַיְתֵי בְּהֵמָה וְלֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adjusts the plan from step 23 to get around the eating-time problem raised in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that there is no fix for the remaining animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling the extra animal a מותר תודה keeps the eating time of a תודה, and it still needs no loaves.

steps.title: רבי sharply rejects the leftover-offering plan
steps.stepSummary: רבי dismisses לוי's suggestion with strong words, saying it seems to him that the one making it has no brain in his head. The reason for rejecting it comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it seems to me that he has no brain in his skull.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי rejects לוי's second plan very strongly. This line sets up the explanation, which the גמרא gives on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי only shows that he rejects the plan. He has not yet said why. The words are harsh, which tells us he sees an obvious flaw in calling the new animal a מותר תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It seems to me
A brain in his skull, meaning good sense

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking רבי gave no reason. This line is only the reaction, and the explanation of the flaw comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It seems to me
that he has no brain in his skull,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּמְדוּמֶּה אֲנִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מוֹחַ בְּקׇדְקֳדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects לוי's adjusted plan from step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Flat rejection of the suggestion, with the reason still to come.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making the extra animal a מותר תודה solves every problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי sees this plan as clearly flawed, and the reason is explained on the next amud.
